value_stream.name: Garden Center, Live Goods & Plant Nursery Operations

fields.Participants: Garden Ops, Inventory (VS-05), Finance (VS-17.4), LP (VS-23), Vendor (VS-03)

Automation Opportunity: - Mortality-cause capture app; auto write-off with attribution; shrink-trend analytics; vendor-claim auto-draft
Controls: - CTL-667 (ensure controlled execution — Live-Goods Shrink, Markdown, Compliance & Analytics (PA-145.3).)
- CTL-667: dead stock detected daily & written off; cause documented; attributed per terms; vendor-claim filed (VS-90)
Cross-references: - links to VS-05 (inventory), VS-17.4 (finance), VS-23 (LP), VS-90 (claims), W4342 (attribution), W4355 (disposal), W4359 (analytics)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Unattributed-shrink risk**: mortality not attributed → cost falls on BuildRight not liable vendor; mitigated by cause-documentation & vendor-claim
- **Late-write-off risk**: dead stock left on floor → display quality/inventory distortion; mitigated by daily detection & periodic write-off
System Touchpoints: - Inventory (VS-05); finance/GL (VS-17.4); LP/shrink (VS-23); vendor claims (VS-90); consignment (VS-45)
Time Estimate: - Detection folded into W4345; write-off periodic

steps.activity: Garden staff detect dead/unsellable plants, document cause (care, transit, vendor-quality, pest/disease), and segregate for disposition (W4355) or vendor-claim (W4338)
Inventory/Finance write off the dead stock from inventory (VS-05) at cost, attribute to BuildRight/consignor/vendor per terms (W4342), and post shrink
LP/Finance analyze shrink trends (by store/cause/vendor), file vendor claims (VS-90), and feed prevention (care, sourcing, transit)

fields.Participants: Garden Ops, Pricing (VS-01.2), Finance (VS-17.4), Marketing (VS-14), Inventory (VS-05)

Automation Opportunity: - Health-grade → markdown auto-suggest; age-based markdown trigger; clearance/donation workflow; RA leakage detection
Controls: - CTL-667 (ensure controlled execution — Live-Goods Shrink, Markdown, Compliance & Analytics (PA-145.3).)
- CTL-667: decline-markdown ladder applied daily; clearance before disposal; margin RA-monitored (VS-118)
Cross-references: - links to VS-01.2/VS-64 (pricing/markdown), VS-05 (inventory), VS-17.4 (finance), VS-118 (RA), W4341 (ladder), W4353 (shrink), W4355 (disposal/donation)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Late-markdown risk**: decline un-marked → mortality instead of recovery revenue; mitigated by daily decline-markdown
- **Recovery-missed risk**: aging stock disposed instead of cleared/donated; mitigated by clearance/donation-before-disposal
Time Estimate: - Daily markdown folded into care; clearance periodic

steps.activity: Garden Ops apply the decline-markdown ladder (W4341) as plants age/stress — health-grade → markdown level, prioritizing sell-through before mortality
Pricing/Marketing set clearance mechanics (bundle, multi-buy, donation-before-disposal) to maximize recovery of aging stock
Finance/RA track markdown margin impact, detect over/under-markdown, and feed prevention (buy-sizing, care)

fields.Participants: Waste (VS-73), Sustainability (VS-25), Garden Ops, Facilities (VS-138), DENR/Compost partner, ESG (VS-25)

Automation Opportunity: - Disposition-decision (compost/disposal); diversion-tonne tracking; ESG auto-report; contamination exclusion flag
Controls: - CTL-667: pesticide-contaminated material excluded from compost; diversion preferred; outcome documented (VS-25)
Cross-references: - links to VS-73 (waste), VS-25 (sustainability/ESG), VS-138 (facilities), W4353 (shrink), W4356 (pesticide), W4360 (ESG reporting)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Contamination risk**: pesticide-treated plants composted → contaminated compost/environment; mitigated by exclusion of treated material
- **Diversion-missed risk**: green-waste landfilled instead of composted; mitigated by diversion-preference & partner composting

steps.activity: Garden Ops/Waste set the green-waste disposition — on-site composting, partner composting, organic-waste collection, or (last resort) disposal — preferring diversion
Garden Ops/Waste process dead/unsellable plants to the chosen channel, exclude chemically-treated/pesticide-contaminated material from compost, and document
Sustainability/ESG track diversion tonnes, compost output, and the disposal outcome for ESG reporting (VS-25) and the circular economy

fields.Participants: HSE (VS-24), Compliance (VS-22), Garden Staff, DG/Hazmat (VS-114), FPA, DENR, Facilities (VS-138)
fields.Trigger: Pesticide use (W4347); chemical storage; compliance cycle

Automation Opportunity: - FPA-registration check at procurement; application-log app; SDS access; spill/exposure incident workflow
Controls: - CTL-667: FPA-registered pesticides only; PPE used; application documented; storage compliant (VS-114); incidents reported
Cross-references: - links to VS-24 (HSE), VS-22 (compliance), VS-114 (DG/hazmat), VS-137 (SDS), W4347 (treatment), W4355 (contamination exclusion)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Exposure risk**: unsafe pesticide handling → staff/customer/environment exposure; mitigated by FPA-product + PPE + label-rate
- **Compliance risk**: unregistered pesticide/improper storage → FPA/DENR violation; mitigated by FPA-registered-only & storage standard

steps.activity: HSE/Compliance set the pesticide/agrochemical handling standard — FPA (Fertilizer & Pesticide Authority)-registered products only, SDS access, storage (segregation/ventilation per VS-114), application limits, PPE
Garden staff apply pesticides per label/FPA, use PPE, store/dispose safely, and document application (product/rate/date)
HSE/Compliance audit handling/storage, manage any spill/exposure incident (VS-114/VS-24), and ensure FPA/DENR reporting

fields.Participants: Compliance (VS-22), Quality (VS-31), Garden Buyer, BPI, Customs (VS-87), Legal (VS-100.3)
fields.Trigger: New live SKU; import; regulatory change

Automation Opportunity: - Restricted-species screening at SKU setup; import-document verification; regulatory-change monitoring; recall workflow
Controls: - CTL-667: restricted/invasive species prohibited; BPI/CITES permits verified; inadvertent stock recalled
Cross-references: - links to VS-22 (compliance), VS-31 (quality), VS-87 (customs), VS-100.3 (legal), VS-01 (merch), W4338 (phytosanitary), VS-89 (recall)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Invasive-species risk**: restricted/invasive plant sold → environmental harm + BPI/DA violation; mitigated by assortment screening & prohibited-sourcing
- **CITES risk**: endangered flora traded without permit → CITES violation; mitigated by CITES permit verification for imports
System Touchpoints: - Compliance (VS-22); quality (VS-31); customs (VS-87); legal (VS-100.3); merchandising (VS-01); master data (VS-29)

steps.activity: Compliance/Garden screen the assortment & imports against restricted/invasive-species lists (BPI/DA, CITES for endangered flora), and prohibit sourcing of restricted species
Quality/Customs verify documentation for imported live plants (BPI import permit, phytosanitary W4338, CITES where applicable) at clearance (VS-87)
Compliance/Legal monitor regulatory change, recall/remove any inadvertently stocked restricted species, and respond to BPI inquiry

fields.Frequency: Frequent cycle count (live-goods drift faster than hard goods)
fields.Participants: Inventory (VS-05), Garden Ops, Store Ops (VS-07), Finance (VS-17.4), LP (VS-23)

workflows.name: Live-Goods Inventory Accuracy, Cycle Count & Reconciliation

Automation Opportunity: - Live-goods cycle-count app by health-zone; variance auto-investigation; accuracy dashboard; theft-pattern analytics
Controls: - CTL-667: live-goods cycle-counted at higher frequency; variance investigated; loss attributed
Cross-references: - links to VS-05 (inventory), VS-17.4 (finance), VS-23 (LP), VS-07 (store), W4353 (shrink/write-off), W4359 (analytics)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Accuracy-drift risk**: live-goods count drifts (mortality/decline) faster than hard-goods cycle; mitigated by higher-frequency live-goods count
- **Variance-attribution risk**: variance cause unclear (mortality vs theft); mitigated by investigation SOP & LP

steps.activity: Inventory/Garden Ops set live-goods cycle-count frequency (higher than hard-goods weekly, given mortality/drift) and the count method (by health-zone/SKU)
Garden staff/Inventory execute the count, reconcile to system (VS-05), investigate variance (mortality un-written W4353, theft VS-23, scan-error), and adjust
Finance/LP analyze accuracy/variance trends, attribute loss, and feed prevention (care, write-off timeliness, security)

fields.Participants: Merchandising (VS-01), Finance (VS-17.4), Garden Ops, Marketing (VS-14), Supply (VS-02)

workflows.name: Garden Center Performance, Sell-Through & Margin Analytics

Automation Opportunity: - Integrated category-KPI dashboard (sell-through/margin/shrink/turn); perishability-adjusted margin; seasonal-ROI analytics
Controls: - CTL-667 (ensure controlled execution — Live-Goods Shrink, Markdown, Compliance & Analytics (PA-145.3).)
- CTL-667: category KPIs reviewed monthly; perishability-adjusted margin tracked; improvement prioritized
Cross-references: - links to VS-01 (merch), VS-17.4 (finance), VS-02 (supply), VS-14 (marketing), VS-28 (BI), W4337 (plan), W4353 (shrink), W4360 (ESG)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Margin-erosion risk**: markdown/shrink eroding margin unflagged; mitigated by post-markdown/shrink margin tracking
- **Sub-optimization risk**: sell-through optimized while margin/care-cost ignored; mitigated by integrated category-KPI view

steps.activity: Garden Buyer/Analytics consolidate category KPIs — sell-through %, gross margin (post-markdown/shrink), shrink/mortality %, inventory-turn, attach-rate, seasonal-event ROI
Merch/Strategy benchmark vs category target & traffic/attach role, identify improvement (assortment, care, sourcing, markdown), and prioritize actions
Garden Buyer/Finance report category contribution & the perishability-adjusted margin, and feed the next seasonal plan (W4337/W4344)

fields.Participants: Sustainability (VS-25), Garden Buyer, ESG, Marketing (VS-14), Compliance (VS-22), Strategy (VS-33)

Automation Opportunity: - Sustainable-sourcing attribute/label; pollinator-native share analytics; ESG auto-feed; customer-facing sustainability content
Controls: - CTL-667 (ensure controlled execution — Live-Goods Shrink, Markdown, Compliance & Analytics (PA-145.3).)
- CTL-667: sustainable sourcing preferences applied; bee-harm reduction; diversion reported (VS-25)
Cross-references: - links to VS-25 (sustainability/ESG), VS-01 (merch), VS-14 (marketing), VS-22 (compliance), VS-36/VS-21 (governance), W4355 (diversion), W4359 (performance)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Bee-harm risk**: neonicotinoid-treated plants harm pollinators → reputational/ESG exposure; mitigated by bee-harm reduction & labeling
- **Narrative-gap risk**: sustainability effort not reflected in ESG narrative; mitigated by consolidated sustainability reporting

steps.activity: Sustainability/Garden set the live-goods sustainability program — pollinator-friendly/native species promotion, neonicotinoid/bee-harm reduction, peat-reduction, responsible sourcing, and green-waste diversion (W4355)
Garden Buyer/Sourcing implement sustainable sourcing preferences (native/pollinator-friendly, certified sustainable growers, reduced-pesticide), and label/promote to customers
Sustainability/ESG report the live-goods sustainability outcome (native/pollinator share, diversion, reduced-pesticide) into the ESG narrative (VS-25) and board assurance (VS-36/VS-21)
